html:
The capital of Peru, founded by Francisco Pizarro on 18 January 1535 near the mouth of the Rímac River. He called it the City of Kings. The site, on the coast, gave easy contact by sea with Panama and Spain, unlike the old Inca capital of Cusco high in the mountains.

Lima became the seat of the Viceroyalty of Peru, which for two centuries ruled nearly all of Spanish South America. Silver from Potosí passed through its port of Callao. It had an archbishop, a court, a branch of the Inquisition, and from 1551 the University of San Marcos. Its rich churches and convents made it the grandest city in Spanish South America.

Earthquakes struck it again and again, worst of all the earthquake of 1746. Lima's power shrank when new viceroyalties were carved out in the 1700s. It became capital of independent Peru in 1821 and is now one of the largest cities in South America.
